name: RuleCondition.constructor
signature: new imports.rulesConfig.RuleCondition({ individual | programEnrolment | programEncounter | encounter })
use_when: Begin a fluent condition chain over the given entity. Always followed by `.when.<accessor>(...)` and terminated with `.matches()`.

name: RuleCondition.when.valueInEncounter
use_when: Open a clause on a concept's observed value on the current encounter. Argument is a concept UUID string. Chain with .defined / .notDefined / .containsAnswerConceptName / etc.

name: RuleCondition.when.valueInRegistration
use_when: Open a clause on a concept's observed value on the subject's registration form.

name: RuleCondition.containsAnswerConceptName
use_when: Match when the observed value contains the named answer concept(s). Pass one or more answer concept UUIDs.

name: RuleCondition.containsAnyAnswerConceptName
use_when: Match when the observed value contains ANY of the listed answer concepts.

name: RuleCondition.defined
use_when: Match when the observed value is present on the entity. Chain after a `.when.value*` clause.

name: RuleCondition.notDefined
use_when: Match when the observed value is absent. Common for follow-up scheduling gated on 'not yet recorded'.

name: RuleCondition.ageInYears
use_when: Compare the subject's age in years. Comparators: lessThan, greaterThan, lessThanOrEqualTo, greaterThanOrEqualTo, equals.

name: RuleCondition.ageInMonths
use_when: Compare the subject's age in months. Useful for infant scheduling.

name: RuleCondition.and.when
use_when: Chain another clause with AND semantics. `.and` joins the result of everything before it with everything after it in the chain, so do not mix `.and` and `.or` in one chain — see RuleCondition.and_or_grouping.

name: RuleCondition.or.when
use_when: Chain another clause with OR semantics. `.or` joins the result of everything before it with everything after it in the chain, so do not mix `.and` and `.or` in one chain — see RuleCondition.and_or_grouping.

name: RuleCondition.not
use_when: Negate a condition, e.g. to hide a field when an answer is selected: "hide when X is No" is `statusBuilder.show().when.valueInEncounter('X').not.containsAnswerConceptName('No')`. Every answer check (containsAnswerConceptName, containsAnyAnswerConceptName, containsAnswerConceptNameOtherThan, and greaterThan / lessThan on a number) is false while the question is unanswered; a date comparison with a unit treats a blank date as today instead, and `.not` turns that into true, so this keeps the field visible until 'No' is chosen. `containsAnswerConceptName('Yes')` and `containsAnswerConceptNameOtherThan('No')` instead hide the field while the question is unanswered, so they are not the same as "hide when No". `.not` applies to the whole rest of the chain.

name: RuleCondition.and_or_grouping
use_when: Combine AND and OR conditions. A RuleCondition or StatusBuilder chain is evaluated from the right: each `.and` / `.or` (and `.not`) applies to the whole rest of the chain, so `A.and.B.or.C.and.D` means A && (B || (C && D)), not (A && B) || (C && D). For any grouping that mixes AND and OR, build one RuleCondition per condition or per same-join group, call `.matches()` on each, and combine the booleans with JavaScript && / || in exactly the intent's bracket structure, without repeating a condition in several groups.

name: RuleCondition.matches
use_when: Terminate the condition chain. Returns a boolean ready to gate a scheduleBuilder.add(...).
